claims.claim: The current Knesset OData service is v4 at https://knesset.gov.il/OdataV4/ParliamentInfo/.
The older v3 endpoint at https://knesset.gov.il/Odata/ParliamentInfo.svc/ is still up but does not expose vote tables.
KNS_PlenumVote is exposed in v4 with fields including Id, VoteDateTime, VoteTitle, VoteMethodDesc, VoteStatusCode, IsNoConfidenceInGov.

claims.claim: KNS_PlenumVoteResult is exposed in v4 with MkId (not PersonID), VoteID, ResultCode, ResultDesc, FirstName, LastName.
ResultCode is not a 1=for/2=against/3=abstain mapping: live rows carry ResultCode 7 for 'בעד' and 8 for 'נגד'. Read ResultDesc, not ResultCode.

The v4 service accepts the OData v4 contains(Field,'text') filter syntax (v3 used substringof('text', Field)). The Hebrew literal must be percent-encoded in the request URL; unencoded Hebrew silently returns an empty value array.
KNS_IsraelLawClassificiation is misspelled in the upstream API (double 'i'); the correctly-spelled name returns 404.
The Knesset has 120 seats, unchanged since 1949.
The electoral threshold is 3.25% of valid votes since the March 2014 amendment; was 2% before.
Seat allocation uses the Bader-Ofer method (modified D'Hondt, equivalent to Hagenbach-Bischoff).
PositionID 43 = male MK, 61 = female MK, 45 = PM, 39 = male Minister, 57 = female Minister, 41 = Committee Chair, 42 = Committee Member, 122/123 = Knesset Speaker (m/f).
claims.raw_snippet: PositionID lexicon from KNS_Position: 43=חבר הכנסת, 61=חברת הכנסת, 45=ראש הממשלה, 39=שר, 57=שרה, 41=יו"ר ועדה, 42=חבר ועדה, 122/123=יושב/ת–ראש הכנסת.

claims.claim: PositionID 54 records faction membership (חבר/ת סיעה), NOT MK status. Filtering by 54 alone to list MKs is incorrect.
claims.raw_snippet: PositionID 54 = חבר/ת סיעה (gender-neutral faction-member designation), separate from 43/61 (MK male/female).

claims.claim: Coalition / opposition split after the 2022 election: 64 vs 56.
Meretz received 3.16% of valid votes in 2022 (below threshold, 0 seats); Balad received 2.91% (below threshold, 0 seats).
The 25th Knesset was sworn in on November 15, 2022.
The next Knesset election (26th Knesset) must be held no later than 27 October 2026.
The 2024 Israeli municipal elections were held on 27 February 2024 in 242 localities, with a second round two weeks later on 10 March 2024 in 35 of them.
claims.raw_snippet: On February 27, 2024, elections were held in 242 localities throughout Israel; two weeks later, on March 10, there was a second round in 35 of them. [1]

claims.claim: 11 localities in northern and southern Israel had their municipal elections postponed to November 2024 due to wartime evacuation.
claims.raw_snippet: Elections would have been held in 253 localities on the original date; but in 11 of them in northern and southern Israel, whose residents had been evacuated because of the war, the elections were postponed and are now scheduled for November 2024.

claims.claim: votes.gov.il no longer resolves; the live Central Elections Committee site is bechirot.gov.il.
Central Elections Committee election results are published on data.gov.il under dataset 'votes-knesset' for Knessets 16-25.
Bill status code 118 = approved in third reading (became law); 108 = preparation for first reading; 125 = rejected; full list via KNS_Status?$filter=TypeID eq 5.
claims.raw_snippet: 118 = approved third reading; 108 = preparation for first reading; 125 = rejected

claims.claim: KNS_CommitteeSession StatusID 193 = cancelled session. Filter with StatusID ne 193 unless cancelled sessions are wanted.
Knesset number 0 in the Knesset data is the Provisional State Council (מועצת המדינה הזמנית), plenum 15 May 1948 to 14 February 1949.
Hasadna's knesset-data project at github.com/hasadna/knesset-data mirrors Knesset internal databases (including vote tables) to CSV/parquet dumps.

The votes-knesset dataset is published by the Knesset (bard@knesset.gov.il) as a set of CSV resources. The per-file character encoding is NOT documented by the publisher and the download endpoints are behind a JS challenge, so the skill tells the agent to detect the encoding rather than asserting Windows-1255 for specific Knesset numbers.
Pre-2014, the Israeli electoral threshold was 2%.
claims.raw_snippet: Until 1992, that threshold was 1% of all votes cast; parties falling under that requirement were not granted seats. The threshold was raised to 1.5% for the 1992 election, and to 2% for the 2003 election. The new Governance Law would raise it to 3.25%, among other measures.

claims.claim: Surplus-vote agreements (heskemei odafim) allow two parties to be treated as one bloc for the leftover-seat allocation round only.

A second round was held on 10 March 2024 in 35 of the 242 localities. The IDI analysis does not state the vote share a mayoral candidate must clear to avoid a runoff, so the skill no longer asserts a percentage.
claims.raw_snippet: two weeks later, on March 10, there was a second round in 35 of them.
